Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Were kicking off a small pilot for embedding Redwood Inference behind our on-prem VPC (Airline-Pilot site) and Im collecting a short architecture review so our infra and security teams can sign off.

Attached: acme-network-drawings.pdf (CIDR, on-prem router details, peering info).

Couple of items wed like your input on before we schedule a review meeting:
- Control plane placement: can Redwood run a private control plane that still lets us manage rollouts, or do you require any outbound control-plane endpoints?
- Data plane isolation: recommendations for subnets / NICs for model-serving pods and KV caches to limit blast radius.
- Egress & auditability: we need fully auditable egress paths and retention of request logs for 365 days.
- Throughput and MTU assumptions for the cross-connect (we expect sustained 2 Gbps).

Are you available for a 30-45m architecture review the week of Oct 26? If so, please loop in your infra lead and any network diagrams youd like us to review.

Hi Olivia — thanks, this is clear and very helpful. Wed love to run the architecture review. Proposed approach:

Agenda (30-40m):
1) Quick run through your attached topology and constraints (10m)
2) Control plane options & implications (Redwood-managed vs. customer-hosted private control plane) (10m)
3) Data plane demarcation, subnets, and egress patterns (10m)

Preliminary notes from our side (will flesh out on the call):
- Control plane: we support a private control plane deployment that keeps orchestration endpoints inside a customer VPC (no public control-plane egress required); option to proxy telemetry to our console if desired.
- Data plane: recommend dedicated subnets for model workers + separate subnets for KV cache & stateful volumes; use secondary ENIs for network separation where supported.
- Egress: we can route all egress through your managed egress proxy (recommended) or via a NAT gateway with VPC flow logs shipped to your SIEM.

Im attaching a short reference appendix (redwood-vpc-reference-appendix-2026-10.pdf) with common CIDR layouts and our usual NAT/proxy recommendations so your team can review ahead of the call.

Looping in a few notes for the call and attaching a quick sketch (redwood-onprem-controlplane-dataplane-sketch.v1.png). High-level questions to validate with Acme:

- Control plane topology: we can deploy a private control plane stack inside the customer VPC (control API endpoints on private subnets) or host a dedicated control-plane in our partner region with mTLS to an egress proxy. For their compliance posture, customer-hosted private control plane looks preferable.

- Control/data demarcation: recommend three logical tiers: control-plane (private endpoint, admin-only CIDR), data-plane-internal (model-serving nodes, restricted to private subnets), and state/cache tier (KV cache, persistent volumes). Use security groups + network ACLs to strictly limit cross-tier traffic.

- Egress & audit: plan to ship all request logs to a customer S3 bucket (or on-prem SIEM) via a VPC-native collector; retention policy 365d as requested. For network egress, recommend an application-level egress proxy with TLS termination at their edge to centralize inspection; avoid hairpinning across AZs if MTU/throughput constraints are tight.

Operational considerations:
- IP planning: request exact service CIDR to avoid overlap.
- Throughput: our default worker images assume jumbo frames disabled; we should validate MTU across their cross-connect for steady 2Gbps.
- DR/HA: if they want failover to a DR site, well need distinct CIDRs and routing rules.

Attaching sketch + will bring this up on the call.

Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone for the time on the call today — quick summary and action items from the architecture review so Acme can proceed with internal sign-off:

Decisions made
- Control plane: customer-hosted private control plane deployed inside Acmes VPC (private subnets). No public control-plane endpoints required.
- Data plane: model workers and autoscaling pools will run in dedicated private subnets in the same VPC; KV cache is scheduled on separate subnets with stateful volumes and restricted SGs.
- Egress / audit: all egress will funnel through Acmes application-level egress proxy. Request logs and audit trails will be delivered to an S3 bucket under Acme account with 365-day retention; VPC flow logs will be forwarded to their SIEM.
- Throughput: confirmed cross-connect needs to sustain 2 Gbps; Karthik to validate MTU assumptions and confirm jumbo-frame policy.

- Karthik: finalize control-plane deployment manifest and update sketch for security groups (due 2026-11-04).
- Neha: prepare audit log delivery test plan and S3 policy template (due 2026-11-05).
- Grace: prepare compliance checklist for their security review (due 2026-11-05).
- Sofia: consolidate notes and post final design doc to shared Drive (link below) and create JIRA-INF-1422 for the pilot rollout tasks.
